message.content: The last common ancestor of lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) was a small, insectivorous mammal that lived during the Paleocene epoch, roughly 70–80 million years ago. This ancestor belonged to the early Laurasiatherian lineage that eventually split into the distinct orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong).
